identity.name: Ethyl methyl cellulose
identity.chemical_class: Modified cellulose ether (mixed alkyl cellulose ether)

function.mechanism: Partially etherified cellulose polymer that hydrates to increase viscosity and helps stabilize emulsions/foams by altering bulk and interfacial behavior.
common_food_categories: general processed foods (EU group-I quantum satis authorization context)
products requiring emulsification or foam stability

adi.basis: EFSA 2018 re-evaluation concluded no need for a numerical ADI for unmodified/modified celluloses including E465; historical SCF/JECFA basis is ADI not specified.

efsa.key_finding: No safety concern at reported uses/use levels for the cellulose group; no genotoxic concern and no carcinogenic properties identified in the group assessment.

adi.basis: WHO/JECFA database lists ADI as NOT SPECIFIED for methyl ethyl cellulose in the modified celluloses group.

concerns.summary: High-dose dietary studies reported reduced body-weight gain at top doses, interpreted as bulk/nutritional effects rather than specific organ toxicity; GI intolerance effects are possible at high intake.
EFSA discussed microbiome/inflammation concerns mainly for E466 literature; this is not direct evidence of E465 harm but indicates class-level mechanistic discussion.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA re-evaluation (2018) found no safety concern at reported uses/use levels for the cellulose group including E465.
JECFA lists ADI as NOT SPECIFIED for methyl ethyl cellulose in the modified celluloses group.
No IARC carcinogenic classification listing was found for methyl ethyl cellulose/CAS 9004-69-7.
Targeted PubMed title/abstract searches found no post-2015 E465-specific toxicology studies beyond the EFSA 2018 re-evaluation record.

adi_exceedance.notes: Exposure figures are generally reported for the combined cellulose group rather than E465 alone. EFSA's highest refined 95th percentile estimate (506 mg/kg bw/day) was below its indicative total exposure range (660-900 mg/kg bw/day); infant FSMP concern discussed in EFSA was tied to E466 data limitations.

risk_assessment.rationale: E465 is approved in major jurisdictions with defined specifications and favorable EFSA/JECFA conclusions, but the evidence base is largely historical/group-based and high-intake GI bulk effects remain plausible.
key_factors: EFSA 2018: no numerical ADI needed; no safety concern at reported uses/use levels (group assessment including E465)
JECFA: ADI NOT SPECIFIED for methyl ethyl cellulose in modified celluloses group
FDA: approved direct food additive under 21 CFR 172.872 with identity/specification/use conditions
No IARC listing/classification found for methyl ethyl cellulose
